instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl, changing the water until it runs clear. Cover it with fresh water and soak for 20 minutes, then drain well.

Meanwhile, slice the onion, chop the tomatoes, mince the ginger and garlic, and slit the green chili down one side, keeping it whole. Chop 3 tbsp of the cilantro and juice the lemon. That should be about 1 tbsp of juice.
Heat the oil in a wide pot with a lid over medium. Add the cashews and fry for 1 minute, until golden. Transfer them to a small plate.

Add the mustard seeds to the same pot. After about 15 seconds they'll start to pop. Add the cumin seeds, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and curry leaves. Stand back, the curry leaves will spatter. Stir for 10 seconds.
Add the onion, the green chili and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is golden.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until they smell fragrant.

Add the turmeric, chili powder and garam masala and stir for 20 seconds. Add the tomatoes. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes have broken down into a thick paste and oil shows at the edges.
Add the drained rice and stir gently for 1 minute, until every grain is coated. Add 3 1/2 cups of water and the remaining 1 tsp salt. Bring it to a boil.
Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 15 minutes. Don't lift the lid. Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice with a fork. Fish out the green chili, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves. Fold in the cilantro, lemon juice and cashews.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
To pack it for lunch: let the rice cool, then pack it in containers. It keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Sprinkle a tablespoon of water over it before microwaving for 1 to 2 minutes, until hot.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes (4.99 from 272 ratings) leads, with Cup of Yum (4.8 from 90) as the second read; Archana's Kitchen shows 5,979 ratings but no average on the page, so it could not lead. Swasthi's is a pressure cooker version; I used a covered pot on the stove with 1 3/4 cups of water per cup of rice. All three build the rice from fried mustard seed and curry leaf, onion and tomato cooked down to a paste, then the rice. I used garam masala as Swasthi does, kept the chili whole so the base stays mild, and skipped the optional mint.
